metaData.originalTitle: [AINews] New AI Infra decacorns: Fireworks， Baseten (with OpenRouter on the way)
metaData.title: [AINews] New AI Infra decacorns: Fireworks， Baseten (with OpenRouter on the way)
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: This AI news roundup covers the rise of AI infrastructure decacorns Fireworks and Baseten, alongside key developments in agent harness engineering, long-horizon reasoning, model architecture updates, and production tooling.
metaData.summary: This edition of AINews from Latent Space highlights the rapid growth of AI inference infrastructure, with Fireworks ($15B) and Baseten ($11B) approaching decacorn status, and OpenRouter raising a $113M Series B. The core theme is that the winning stack for AI agents is now 'model + harness + eval loop', not just a stronger base model. Key technical developments include: DeepSWE as a more realistic coding benchmark, the 'Language Models Need Sleep' paper for context compression, new optimizer work (AMUSE, Muon variants), MiniMax's M3 sparse attention architecture, and Huawei's 'τ scaling' engineering roadmap. The newsletter also covers production tooling updates like vLLM's Rust frontend, W&B's MCP server, and Cloudflare's startups program. On the open model front, Qwen 3.7 Max is positioned as a frontier model, while local inference benchmarks show Qwen3.6 35B A3B achieving 110 tok/s on a 12GB GPU.

mainPoints.point: AI inference infrastructure is rapidly scaling, with Fireworks and Baseten approaching decacorn status.
mainPoints.explanation: Fireworks is reportedly in talks for a $15B valuation (3.75x in 7 months) and Baseten is raising at $11B (2.2x in 3 months), signaling a massive market shift toward inference as a durable platform layer.

mainPoints.point: The winning stack for coding agents is now 'model + harness + eval loop', not just a stronger base model.
mainPoints.explanation: Multiple sources converged on the thesis that context governance, trustworthy memory, and dynamic skill routing are becoming the main differentiators, with DeepSeek, Google, and LangChain all formalizing harness engineering.

mainPoints.point: Long-horizon memory and context compression are resurfacing as core bottlenecks for agents.
mainPoints.explanation: The 'Language Models Need Sleep' paper proposes a sleep-like consolidation phase that converts recent context into persistent fast weights, offering an alternative to ever-growing KV caches for agents with long trajectories.

mainPoints.point: Production serving stacks are seeing meaningful performance improvements, like vLLM's Rust frontend.
mainPoints.explanation: vLLM merged a Rust frontend as a drop-in alternative to the Python API server, achieving ~837 req/s vs ~162 req/s on a preprocess-heavy workload, a 5x improvement.

mainPoints.point: Open-weight models like Qwen3.6 35B A3B are enabling practical local agent workflows.
mainPoints.explanation: Users report running local agents with Qwen3.6 35B A3B at over 100 tok/s on consumer GPUs, enabling workflows like VPS DevOps, document conversion, and automated ticket management.

keyQuotes: The winning stack is now model + harness + eval loop, not just a stronger base model.
DeepSWE is the first code bench that actually aligns with how it feels to use these models coding.
Language Models Need Sleep: a sleep-like consolidation phase where recent context is converted into persistent fast weights before clearing the KV cache.
vLLM merged a Rust frontend... showing ~837 req/s vs ~162 req/s on a preprocess-heavy workload in a single process.
OpenRouter announced a $113M Series B and said weekly volume had grown from 5T to 25T tokens over six months.

relatedArticles.title: Agents that remember: introducing Agent Memory
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Cloudflare announces the private beta of Agent Memory, a managed service that provides AI agents with persistent, context-aware memory by extracting and retrieving knowledge from conversations, solving the problem of context rot without overfilling the context window.

relatedArticles.title: Higher usage limits for Claude and a compute deal with SpaceX
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Anthropic announces higher usage limits for Claude Code and API, and a new compute partnership with SpaceX to access over 300 megawatts of capacity.

relatedArticles.title: Retrieval After RAG: Hybrid Search， Agents， and Database Design — Simon Hørup Eskildsen of Turbopuffer
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Turbopuffer is a cloud-native search engine for unstructured data that leverages a tiered storage architecture (S3 to NVMe) to provide cost-efficient, high-concurrency retrieval for RAG and agentic workflows.

relatedArticles.title: Cursor's Third Era: Cloud Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article explores Cursor's transition into the 'Cloud Agent' era, where AI agents utilize full virtual machines and 'Computer Use' to build, test, and demonstrate software autonomously.

relatedArticles.title: Why Anthropic Thinks AI Should Have Its Own Computer — Felix Rieseberg of Claude Cowork & Claude Code Desktop
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Felix Rieseberg discusses why Anthropic believes the future of AI lies in trusted task execution through local-first agent workflows, where AI has its own computer to work with rather than just chat interfaces.

relatedArticles.title: Extreme Harness Engineering for Token Billionaires: 1M LOC， 1B toks/day， 0% human code， 0% human review — Ryan Lopopolo， OpenAI Frontier & Symphony
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: OpenAI's Ryan Lopopolo introduces 'Harness Engineering,' a radical workflow where a 1M LOC codebase was built with 0% human-written code and 1B tokens spent daily.

relatedArticles.title: Notion’s Token Town: 5 Rebuilds, 100+ Tools, MCP vs CLIs and the Software Factory Future — Simon Last & Sarah Sachs of Notion
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Notion's AI engineering leads, Sarah Sachs and Simon Last, detail the multi-year, iterative journey to build Custom Agents, sharing insights on product timing, team culture, evaluation philosophy, and the vision for agent-native collaboration and software factories.

relatedArticles.title: How AI is Changing Software Engineering: A Conversation with Gergely Orosz
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: In this interview, Gergely Orosz discusses the emergence of 'Token Maxing' in big tech, the evolving role of software engineers in the AI era, the massive internal AI infrastructure investments by companies like Meta and Uber, and the rationale behind these strategic moves.

relatedArticles.title: The History and Future of AI at Google: A Conversation with Sundar Pichai
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai discusses the company's AI evolution, vertical integration strategy, upcoming 2026 infrastructure bottlenecks, and the transformation of search into an agent-based orchestration layer.

relatedArticles.title: Cursor and SpaceX Partner to Scale AI Coding with Stargate-Class Infrastructure
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Cursor CEO Michael Truell announces a strategic partnership with SpaceX to leverage massive compute infrastructure for scaling the Cursor Composer and building advanced coding models.
